cards.back:
A comparison that uses the word like or as.
Bahasa Indonesia: simile, perumpamaan
Example: She ran like the wind. This is a simile.
cards.say: simile. A comparison that uses the word like or as. She ran like the wind. This is a simile.

cards.back:
A comparison that says one thing is another.
Bahasa Indonesia: metafora
Example: The classroom was a zoo. This is a metaphor.
cards.say: metaphor. A comparison that says one thing is another. The classroom was a zoo. This is a metaphor.

cards.back:
Giving human actions or feelings to things that are not human.
Bahasa Indonesia: personifikasi
Example: The wind whispered through the trees. This is personification.
cards.say: personification. Giving human actions or feelings to things that are not human. The wind whispered through the trees. This is personification.

cards.back:
Repeating the same sound at the start of nearby words.
Bahasa Indonesia: aliterasi
Example: Peter picked a pot of pickled peppers. This shows alliteration.
cards.say: alliteration. Repeating the same sound at the start of nearby words. Peter picked a pot of pickled peppers. This shows alliteration.

cards.back:
A word that sounds like the noise it describes.
Bahasa Indonesia: onomatope
Example: Buzz, splash and crash are examples of onomatopoeia.
cards.say: onomatopoeia. A word that sounds like the noise it describes. Buzz, splash and crash are examples of onomatopoeia.

cards.back:
A great exaggeration that is not meant to be believed.
Bahasa Indonesia: hiperbola
Example: I have told you a million times. This is hyperbole.
cards.say: hyperbole. A great exaggeration that is not meant to be believed. I have told you a million times. This is hyperbole.

cards.back:
A phrase whose meaning is different from its separate words.
Bahasa Indonesia: idiom
Example: It is raining cats and dogs. This is a famous idiom.
cards.say: idiom. A phrase whose meaning is different from its separate words. It is raining cats and dogs. This is a famous idiom.

cards.back:
Words that create a picture in the reader's mind.
Bahasa Indonesia: citraan
Example: The poet used imagery to describe the golden sunset.
cards.say: imagery. Words that create a picture in the reader's mind. The poet used imagery to describe the golden sunset.

cards.back:
An object that stands for an idea.
Bahasa Indonesia: simbol
Example: A white dove is a symbol of peace.
cards.say: symbol. An object that stands for an idea. A white dove is a symbol of peace.

cards.back:
When the result is the opposite of what you expect.
Bahasa Indonesia: ironi
Example: A fire station burning down is an example of irony.
cards.say: irony. When the result is the opposite of what you expect. A fire station burning down is an example of irony.

cards.back:
Two words with opposite meanings used together.
Bahasa Indonesia: oksimoron
Example: Deafening silence is an oxymoron because the two words clash.
cards.say: oxymoron. Two words with opposite meanings used together. Deafening silence is an oxymoron because the two words clash.

cards.back:
A short, wise saying that many people know.
Bahasa Indonesia: peribahasa
Example: A proverb says that slow and steady wins the race.
cards.say: proverb. A short, wise saying that many people know. A proverb says that slow and steady wins the race.

cards.back:
When words end with the same sound.
Bahasa Indonesia: rima
Example: The words cat and hat make a rhyme because they end alike.
cards.say: rhyme. When words end with the same sound. The words cat and hat make a rhyme because they end alike.

cards.back:
The writer's attitude, shown through word choice.
Bahasa Indonesia: nada
Example: The cheerful tone of the letter made me smile.
cards.say: tone. The writer's attitude, shown through word choice. The cheerful tone of the letter made me smile.

cards.back:
The feeling a piece of writing gives the reader.
Bahasa Indonesia: suasana
Example: The dark forest scene created a tense mood.
cards.say: mood. The feeling a piece of writing gives the reader. The dark forest scene created a tense mood.

cards.back:
A group of lines in a poem, a little like a paragraph.
Bahasa Indonesia: bait
Example: The first stanza of the poem has four lines.
cards.say: stanza. A group of lines in a poem, a little like a paragraph. The first stanza of the poem has four lines.

cards.back:
A section of a song, or a line of poetry.
Bahasa Indonesia: bait (lagu atau puisi)
Example: We sang the first verse of the song together.
cards.say: verse. A section of a song, or a line of poetry. We sang the first verse of the song together.

cards.back:
A line that is repeated in a poem or song.
Bahasa Indonesia: refrain
Example: Everyone joined in the refrain at the end of each verse.
cards.say: refrain. A line that is repeated in a poem or song. Everyone joined in the refrain at the end of each verse.

cards.back:
A joke that uses a word with two meanings.
Bahasa Indonesia: permainan kata, plesetan
Example: Why was the maths book sad? It had too many problems. This is a pun.
cards.say: pun. A joke that uses a word with two meanings. Why was the maths book sad? It had too many problems. This is a pun.

cards.back:
Saying the opposite of what you mean to make fun.
Bahasa Indonesia: sarkasme (sindiran tajam)
Example: Saying Oh, great weather while it pours with rain is sarcasm.
cards.say: sarcasm. Saying the opposite of what you mean to make fun. Saying Oh, great weather while it pours with rain is sarcasm.

cards.back:
The words spoken by characters in a story.
Bahasa Indonesia: dialog
Example: The dialogue in the play made the audience laugh out loud.
cards.say: dialogue. The words spoken by characters in a story. The dialogue in the play made the audience laugh out loud.

cards.back:
Not meant exactly, but used to create a picture or idea.
Bahasa Indonesia: kiasan, bersifat kiasan
Example: A figurative expression makes your writing more colourful and fun.
cards.say: figurative. Not meant exactly, but used to create a picture or idea. A figurative expression makes your writing more colourful and fun.

cards.back:
The voice that tells the story.
Bahasa Indonesia: narator
Example: The narrator introduced each character at the start of the book.
cards.say: narrator. The voice that tells the story. The narrator introduced each character at the start of the book.
